reason: The two quotes state Lambda automatically assumes the execution role when you invoke the function, and the trust policy must specify lambda.amazonaws.com as a trusted service.
The quote states no additional charge for advanced logging controls and continued CloudWatch Logs charges for ingestion and storage.
The quote states Lambda stores code in Amazon S3 and encrypts it at rest.
Under the signature checks performed at deployment, the quote defines a corrupt signature as a code artifact altered since signing.
The quote states code signing can be enabled for existing functions by attaching a code signing configuration.
Under the deployment signature checks, the quote defines a mismatched signature as an artifact signed by a signing profile that is not approved.
The quote states no additional cost for Code Signing and that you pay the standard Lambda price.
The quote states the Code Signing Configuration specifies approved signing profiles and whether to warn or reject deployments if signature checks fail.
The quote states code signing verifies only unaltered code from approved developers is deployed, with AWS Signer signing artifacts and functions verifying signatures at deployment.
The quote states code signing is currently only available for functions packaged as ZIP archives.

The quote supports that the default maximum concurrent execution limit applies at the account level and that per-function limits can be set, but the qualifier adjustable=true is not stated in this quote or its context.
The quote states deployment as .zip file archives or container images, both with the same execution environment, scaling and operational simplicity.
The quote states that on exceeding the retry policy for asynchronous invocations the event is placed in a configured DLQ, and without one it may be rejected.
The quote states an Amazon SQS queue or an Amazon SNS topic can be configured as the dead letter queue.

The quote states the per-invocation timeout remains 15 minutes, durable functions suspend and resume across invocations, and with asynchronous invocation the durable execution timeout can extend up to one year.
The quote states each checkpointed operation can store up to 256 KB and the limit applies to the data returned from the operation.
The quote states durable functions use the same account-level concurrency pool and concurrency slots are released during waits.
The quote states durable functions currently support JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and Java.
The quote states for on-demand functions using the durable execution SDK wait capabilities there are no compute charges during suspension.

The quote supports execution timeout up to 1 year and retention up to 90 days, but the adjacent FAQ answer in the context ties the one-year timeout to invoking durable functions asynchronously; the claim drops that condition.

The quote states when to use durable functions (Lambda programming model, local testing, preferred language) and Step Functions (visual workflow design, cross-team visibility, native integrations, zero-maintenance infrastructure).
The quote states Node.js or Python code triggered by CloudFront requests at viewer request, origin request/response and before responding to the end-user.
The quote states existing functions can be associated with CloudFront events if they satisfy the Lambda@Edge service requirements and limits.
The quote supports associating a function version with CloudFront requests, but says nothing about $LATEST; the claim's 'not $LATEST' goes beyond the quote.
The quote states Lambda@Edge supports Node.js and Python for global invocation by CloudFront events.
The quote states Lambda@Edge is optimized for latency-sensitive use cases with globally distributed viewers, with the needed information available at the edge within the function and request.
Under the question whether Lambda supports environment variables, the quote answers yes and says they can be created and modified from the console, CLI or SDKs.
The quote states some services such as S3 invoke the function directly and Lambda can poll resources in services that do not publish events.
The quote states permissions to other resources are granted via an IAM role that Lambda assumes while executing the function, keeping control of which resources it can use.
The quote states synchronously invoked functions respond with an exception on failure.
The quote states replication and redundancy for high availability of the service and functions, with no maintenance windows or scheduled downtimes for either.

The quote says you 'can' invoke over HTTPS by defining a RESTful API with API Gateway; the claim's wording 'To invoke over HTTPS you define' presents it as the required way, which the quote does not state.
The quote states that with the invoke API only the function owner or another account granted permission can invoke the function.
The quote states each function runs in its own isolated environment with its own resources and file system view.
The quote lists the same seven native languages and the Runtime API for any additional language.
The quote states any code (frameworks, SDKs, libraries) can be packaged as a Lambda Layer and shared across multiple functions.
The quote states Service Quotas is used to request an increase of the concurrent execution limit, which the context scopes per account per region.
The quote states you can set which CloudWatch log group Lambda sends logs to, aggregating logs from multiple functions in one place.
Under the advanced logging controls question, the quote states logs can be captured in JSON structured format without your own logging libraries.
The quote states log level filtering can be controlled without making any code changes.
